history.content: Is there a reason to buy a 0% yield bond?

Yes, there are reasons to buy a 0% yield bond. They can be desirable for some individuals due to the nature of their capital gains. When sold, these bonds typically yield capital gains, which are often taxed at a more favorable rate than income in many countries, including the US and Canada. This is especially true when holding these investments in corporations  but  as an individual you're likely better off in a low-yield cash account.
I do not have specific information low-yield cash account.
Could you tell me the main reason why some people go with lower interest accounts?

Yes, one of the main reasons why some people choose lower interest accounts it is for convenience of having the money in the same institution with other accounts (like checking, auto loans, credit cards, etc.) with their local bank. As savings accounts are regulated by law to only allow 6 transfers out per month, so for people that need to make withdrawals more frequently, that can also be a factor. Also,some accounts have limitations in case a bank goes belly up and you have a higher amount in the account (more than the insured amount).
The interest rates are so low!

The interest rates are at historic lows because governments want people to use their money to improve the economy by spending or investing rather than saving. Their idea is that by consuming or investing you will help to create jobs that will employ people who will spend or invest their pay, and so on. Some people  think that interest rates should not remain so low. However,when you raise the rates, banks are induced to loan money and forces  people to become savers instead of spenders. Not good for the economy.
What is the best time to buy a house?

A depressed housing market might be the best time to buy a house. There are foreclosures where banks are letting houses go for half of their standard value, and are offering some of the lowest interest rates. But if the real state agents selling homes are tripping over each other, is a sign that is not a good time to buy a home. It is important to note that a wise time to buy homes today where you will be able to rent them out tomorrow.
Where are the best neighborhood to buy a house?
I don't have specific information about the best neighborhoods to buy a house .
Could you tell which areas I could buy in case I want to invest in the future?

Extremely cheap areas in proximity to urban wealth are the best places to speculate in terms of large-scale real-estate developments. A golf-course developer ideally wants a huge amount of cheap land in close proximity to some combination of wealthy retirees, business-executives, or vacationers like a farmland on the fringes of urban areas. It is important to note that blighted and depressed suburbs or neighborhoods with lots of abandoned housing are the new under-utilized farmland. You need to have in mind before buy any area for future investment to check the zoning commission  restrictions.

evidence.text: Do not borrow to invest in real estate.  The interest payments will eat up most of your profit (the property management fees might eat up the rest), and you will have significant risk with tenant issues, property value, etc.  Many people have made it work - many also lose everything. Real estate can be a great investment, but you can't even afford a house of your own yet, let alone investment property.  Keep saving up until you have 20% down to buy a house of your own (ideally that you can put on a 15% fixed mortgage), and pay it off as quickly as you can.  Then you can start saving for your first rental property. If that process isn't fast enough for you, you have two options.  Increase your income or reduce your expenses.  There's no shortcut to wealth-building without taking significant risks. At most I would scale back the 401(k) to the 5% match you get, but you should scale that back up once you have enough for a down payment.
